value: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office; prepared by Energetics Incorporated (2012). Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprint Definitions and Assumptions. Companion document to the 2006 MECS Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (October 2012), 8 pp.

Methodology companion to the 2006 MECS footprint diagrams (doe_2012_001); no technology parameters. How the footprint is built from MECS: definitions of each flow and the assumptions behind it (boiler, CHP and end-use efficiencies and losses, steam distribution, machine-drive split, adjustments to MECS fuel data, feedstock treatment). The methodology needed to reproduce or extend the footprints from MECS tables. Copied 2026-10-08 from the modeller's N:\CIMS\Sources\Technologies\EIA MECS\2006 folder (download name footprints_assumptions_definitions_2012.pdf). Reviewed 2026-10-08 for mecs_footprint_metrics.py. What can be reproduced from MECS: fuel and electricity by end use (Tables 5.2/5.4, 3.2/3.5); the coke / blast furnace gas adjustment (coke and breeze less the BFG heat content, about two-thirds of Table 3.5 BFG/COG; reproduces the iron and steel footprint coke within 2-18 TBtu); every loss factor, efficiency and the steam end-use shares, which are printed here. Not reproducible: the sector-by-sector rework of MECS 'Other Fuels' (described only in doe_2012 analysis Appendix D as based on other EIA data, published sources and expert discussion; e.g. chemicals 2018 keeps about 120 of MECS's 420 TBtu of unnamed 'other'), CHP outputs (from EIA-923), and the machine-drive subsystem shares (ORNL 2002 motor study, not printed). mecs_footprint_metrics.py applies the coke adjustment and balances 'other' to the footprint fuel total. 2006 specifics: one 80% boiler efficiency for all sectors; CHP efficiency by sector from EIA-906/920/923; grid efficiency 31.6%.
